claims.text: In Ti-Zr-Nb-Mo-W high-entropy alloys, superconducting behavior is governed by the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
The Fermi-level density of states is modulated by valence electron count.
Small increases or decreases in VEC will non-monotonically alter electron-phonon coupling strength.
VEC-induced changes in electron-phonon coupling will shift Tc predictably.
An equiatomic Ti-Zr-Nb-Mo-W alloy can serve as a single-phase random solid-solution starting material.
Composition can be varied by ±2–3 at.% between the selected transition metals while retaining every element above 5 at.% and preserving the solid-solution phase.
Melt-quenching followed by controlled annealing will produce equilibrium phase formation in the proposed alloy series.
BCS superconductivity is sensitive to the density of states at the Fermi energy.
Changing VEC changes the Fermi-level density of states in the proposed Ti-Zr-Nb-Mo-W system.
Changes in the Fermi-level density of states alter electron-phonon coupling and the superconducting pairing potential.
Tc will have a non-monotonic dependence on VEC, with a maximum at an optimal composition.
Moving VEC away from the optimum will lower Tc.
Tunneling or photoemission measurements will reveal systematic Fermi-level density-of-states changes corresponding to the compositional VEC adjustments.
The baseline Tc is characteristic of both the baseline VEC and its disorder level.
The proposed interpretation is applicable only while the alloys remain single-phase, compositionally homogeneous solid solutions with no major lattice-structure change.
Disorder can suppress superconductivity near an Anderson quantum phase transition and may confound the effect attributed to VEC.
A lack of non-monotonic Tc variation with VEC, or a lack of systematic density-of-states modulation with VEC, would falsify the proposed VEC-to-density-of-states mechanism.
